title: Learning trombone then trumpet; teachers; ragtime and marches
summary: Pope began briefly on trombone, switched to trumpet, took lessons from other teachers, and played ragtime and Sousa marches against visiting bands at Carnival.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: No. No. He plays sax, clarinet, and trumpet. Yes, sir. Three instruments. When you started in music, did you start right on the cornet first?
No, I had what you call a vowel trombone. Oh, you did. That was very short, just probably a month or so, you know, I changed to the trumpet.
Did your father give you lessons?
No, not my father. By the name of Mr. Norman Cox, he's dead now. And the punk brunette, they were teachers back in those days. Yes. And I felt one of those fellows.
In fact, most all of us did.
What was the music like when you, the first music you remember hearing the band play? Did they play those popular pieces in charge of jazzy and time? That's right. Kind of jazzy time.

Ragtime. Ragtime back in those days, you know. Even when you were a boy. We played all the famous marches, quite a bit of Susan's marches. Yes. All heavy marches, you know. The kick that we got out of playing those kind of things, when they bring those bands from St. Louis, Chicago, down in the for Carnival, you know, we used to Carnival marches out of the government street. Yes. And we'd meet the little 14th piece band and put them out of commission, you know. Used to blast away, you know. They'd have probably 40, 50 million in the band.
